title: Watch your app come alive
content:
## What you'll get

In the next few minutes, you'll watch Emergent's AI agent turn your description into a real, working app - no coding required.

## The agent asks a few setup questions

After you submit your prompt, the agent needs to confirm a few choices before it starts building. You'll see questions like:

**Which API key to use?**  
The **Universal Key** is already included with your account and covers most builds. If you have your own OpenAI or Anthropic key, you can provide it here - but for your first build, just choose the Universal Key.

**Does your app need user accounts?**  
For a personal tracker or tool, you might skip authentication. For anything with multiple users, the agent can add Emergent Auth (built-in, zero setup) or connect to a service you already use.

**Start building now, or explain the plan first?**  
- **Start building now** gets you to a working app fastest.
- **Explain the plan first** shows you what the agent intends to build so you can adjust before credits are spent.

For your first time, **"explain the plan first"** is safer - you'll see the full picture and can refine before work begins.

<Callout type="info" title="Video coming soon">
A short screen recording will go here.
</Callout>

<Callout type="success" title="Adjust the plan before work begins">
Choosing "explain the plan first" lets you review and adjust what the agent intends to build before it starts. Credits are drawn down once the agent starts generating code, running tests and deploying (see [How credits work](/how-credits-work)).
</Callout>

## Watch the agent work

Once you confirm, the agent begins. You'll see a live stream of steps in the chat:

- **Planning** - breaking your idea into components and features  
- **Scaffolding** - creating the project structure and installing tools  
- **Implementation** - writing the code that makes your app work  
- **Testing** - checking for errors automatically  
- **Deployment** - getting everything ready to run

The first build usually takes a few minutes. The agent works autonomously - you don't need to approve every step.

<Callout type="note" title="Checkpoints save your progress">
The platform automatically saves snapshots of your app as the agent works. If anything goes wrong or you want to undo a change later, you can roll back to any earlier checkpoint. Your work is never lost.
</Callout>

## Your first preview

As soon as the agent finishes, a **live preview** appears. This is your app, running in real time. You can click through it, test features, and see exactly what you built.

The preview updates automatically whenever the agent makes changes - no refresh needed.

<Callout type="info" title="Screenshot coming soon">
Screenshot to be added.
</Callout>

Try interacting with your app like a real user would: tap buttons, fill in forms, navigate between pages. If something doesn't look or work the way you expected, just describe the change in chat and the agent will fix it.

<Callout type="warning" title="Preview vs deployed app">
The preview is separate from your deployed app. Changes you see in the preview won't appear in production until you explicitly deploy (or redeploy). The preview is your testing playground; deployment is when you publish for real.
</Callout>

## If something looks wrong

If the agent stops or the preview doesn't match what you asked for, you have options:

- **Describe the issue in chat** and the agent will iterate. Be specific: "Move the search bar to the top" works better than "the layout is off."
- **Roll back to an earlier checkpoint** if a recent change broke something that was working. Open the History panel in the sidebar, pick a snapshot, and restore it.
- **Ask the agent to explain what it built** if you're not sure why something works the way it does.

The agent learns from your feedback and adjusts as you go.

<Callout type="tip">
Start small. Your first build should be something you can describe in a few sentences. You can always add more features later - it's faster to build in layers than to fix a big, complicated first attempt.
</Callout>
